questions.text: एक आवृतबीजी भ्रूण-कोश इस संरचना के अन्दर अवस्थित होता है :
questions.text_english: An angiosperm embryo sac is located within the :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Nucellus. In angiosperms, the embryo sac (female gametophyte) develops within the nucellus, which is the nutritive tissue of the ovule. The megaspore mother cell undergoes meiosis within the nucellus to form the embryo sac. Option A (Placenta) is the region where ovules are attached; Option B (Megasporangium) is essentially the ovule but the embryo sac is specifically within the nucellus part of it; Option D (Ovary) is the broader structure that contains ovules.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) बीजाण्डकाय है। आवृतबीजियों में, भ्रूण-कोश (मादा युग्मकोद्भिद) बीजाण्डकाय के अंदर विकसित होता है, जो बीजांड का पोषक ऊतक है।

questions.text: स्तंभ I की मदों का मिलान स्तंभ II से कीजिए और नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही सुमेलित विकल्प का चयन कीजिए : स्तंभ I (क्रॉस) — स्तंभ II (फीनोटाइप अनुपात) : 1. मेंडलीय एकसंकर (मोनोहाइब्रिड) — (i) 1:2:1 (F2), 2. मेंडलीय द्विसंकर — (ii) 1:1, 3. अपूर्ण प्रभाविता (इंकंप्लीट डोमिनेंस) — (iii) 3:1 (F2), 4. परीक्षार्थ संकरण (एकसंकर) (मोनोहाइब्रिड) — (iv) 9:3:3:1 (F2)
questions.text_english: Match the items in Column I with those in Column II and select the correctly matched option from those given below : Column I (Cross) — Column II (Phenotypic Ratio) : 1. Mendelian monohybrid — (i) 1:2:1 (F2), 2. Mendelian dihybrid — (ii) 1:1, 3. Incomplete dominance — (iii) 3:1 (F2), 4. Test cross (monohybrid) — (iv) 9:3:3:1 (F2)
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C): 1-(iii), 2-(iv), 3-(i), 4-(ii). Mendelian monohybrid cross gives a 3:1 phenotypic ratio in F2. Mendelian dihybrid cross gives a 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio in F2. Incomplete dominance gives a 1:2:1 ratio in F2 because the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype. A test cross (monohybrid) always gives a 1:1 ratio because the unknown individual is crossed with a homozygous recessive.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है: 1-(iii), 2-(iv), 3-(i), 4-(ii)। मेंडलीय एकसंकर क्रॉस में F2 में 3:1 फीनोटाइप अनुपात, द्विसंकर में 9:3:3:1, अपूर्ण प्रभाविता में 1:2:1, और परीक्षार्थ संकरण में 1:1 अनुपात प्राप्त होता है।

questions.text: मानव में, द्वितीयक अंडक का अर्धसूत्री विभाजन तब पूर्ण होता है जब :
questions.text_english: In humans, the secondary oocyte completes meiotic division when :

options.A: यह गर्भाशय के अंत:स्तर में अंतरोंपित हो जाता है।
options.B: यह परिपक्व ग्राफी पुटक से मोचित होता है।
options.D: अग्रपिंडक के एंज़ाइम ज़ोना पेलुसिडा (पारदर्शी अंडावरण) का भंजन करते हैं।

options_english.A: it gets implanted in the uterine endometrium.
options_english.B: it is released from the matured Graafian follicle.
options_english.C: it is penetrated by the sperm cell.
options_english.D: acrosomal enzymes break down the zona pellucida.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) — when it is penetrated by the sperm cell. The secondary oocyte is arrested in Meiosis II (metaphase II) after ovulation. It is only upon penetration by a sperm cell that the secondary oocyte is stimulated to complete Meiosis II, releasing the ovum and a second polar body. Option B is incorrect because at ovulation the secondary oocyte is released but meiosis II is not yet complete; Options A and D describe events that occur either after or separately from the completion of meiosis II.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है — जब शुक्राणु इसमें प्रवेश करता है। द्वितीयक अंडक अर्धसूत्री विभाजन II की मेटाफेज अवस्था में रुका होता है और शुक्राणु के प्रवेश के बाद ही विभाजन II पूर्ण होता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following statements is not true ?

options.A: ह्वेल तथा डॉल्फिन के पक्ष (फ्लिपर्स) समजात अंग हैं।
options.B: समजात अंगों की शारीरिक संरचना तो समान होती है, परन्तु वे भिन्न क्रियाकलाप संपन्न करते हैं।
options.C: समजातता समान पूर्वज परंपराएँ इंगित करती है।
options.D: समजात संरचनाएँ अभिसारी विकास का परिणाम हैं।

options_english.A: Flippers of whales and dolphins are homologous organs.
options_english.B: Homologous organs have similar anatomical structure, but perform different functions.
options_english.D: Homologous structures are a result of convergent evolution.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). Homologous structures are NOT a result of convergent evolution; they are a result of divergent evolution. Homologous organs share a common ancestral origin and similar anatomical structure but may perform different functions in different species — this is divergent evolution. Convergent evolution produces analogous organs (such as wings of insects and birds) which have similar functions but different origins. Options A, B, and C are all true statements about homologous organs.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। समजात संरचनाएँ अभिसारी नहीं बल्कि अपसारी विकास का परिणाम हैं। अभिसारी विकास से समवृत्ति (समानार्थी) अंग बनते हैं।
questions.topic: Homologous and Analogous Organs / Divergent and Convergent Evolution

questions.text: 2 युग्मविकल्पी (दो विशेषकों) वाले जीन के लिए एक समष्टि आनुवंशिक संतुलन/हार्डी-वेनबर्ग संतुलन में होती है (प्रभावी ऐलील 'A' तथा अप्रभावी ऐलील 'a' है)। यदि ऐलील 'A' की आवृत्ति 0·6 है, तो जीनोटाइप 'Aa' की आवृत्ति होगी :
questions.text_english: A population is in genetic equilibrium/Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium for a gene with 2 alleles (dominant allele is 'A' and recessive allele 'a'). If the frequency of allele 'A' is 0·6, then the frequency of genotype 'Aa' is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 0·48. Using the Hardy-Weinberg equation, if p = frequency of allele A = 0·6, then q = frequency of allele a = 1 − 0·6 = 0·4. The frequency of heterozygous genotype Aa = 2pq = 2 × 0·6 × 0·4 = 0·48. The other options are incorrect: 0·21 would be p² for A (actually 0·36), 0·42 is not a standard result, and 0·32 is not correct either.

questions.text: डीएनए अणु की द्विकुंडली संरचना में, रज्जुक होते हैं :
questions.text_english: In the double helical structure of DNA molecule, the strands are :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) anti-parallel and complementary. In the DNA double helix, the two strands run in opposite directions (one 5' to 3' and the other 3' to 5'), making them anti-parallel. The bases on one strand pair specifically with bases on the other strand by hydrogen bonds (A pairs with T, G pairs with C), making them complementary. They are not identical because one strand is the complement of the other.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) प्रति-समानांतर तथा पूरक है। DNA के दोनों रज्जुक विपरीत दिशाओं में चलते हैं और बेस पेयरिंग के कारण एक-दूसरे के पूरक होते हैं।

questions.text: एक 'अनुलेखन इकाई' में, 'समापक' (टर्मिनेटर) इस ओर अवस्थित होता है :
questions.text_english: In a 'transcription unit', the 'terminator' is located towards the :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 3' end of the coding strand. In a transcription unit, transcription proceeds from the 3' end of the template strand to the 5' end (reading direction). The terminator sequence signals the end of transcription and is located at the downstream end — which corresponds to the 3' end of the coding (non-template) strand. The promoter is at the 5' end of the coding strand, while the terminator is at the 3' end of the coding strand.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) कोडिंग रज्जुक के 3' किनारे पर है। अनुलेखन इकाई में, प्रमोटर 5' सिरे पर और समापक (टर्मिनेटर) कोडिंग रज्जुक के 3' सिरे पर होता है।

questions.text: सामान्य दृष्टि वाली स्त्री के पिता वर्णांध हैं। वह स्त्री एक सामान्य दृष्टि वाले पुरुष से विवाह करती है। उनकी संतान के वर्णांध होने का संभाव्य प्रतिशत होगा :
questions.text_english: A woman with normal vision has a colour blind father. She marries a man with normal vision. The percentage chance of their progeny being colour blind is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 25%. Colour blindness is X-linked recessive. The woman's father is colour blind (X^b Y), so she must have inherited one X^b from him; since she has normal vision, her genotype is X^B X^b (carrier). Her husband has normal vision (X^B Y). Their children: daughters — X^B X^B (normal) and X^B X^b (carrier normal); sons — X^B Y (normal) and X^b Y (colour blind). So 25% of total progeny (all sons have 50% chance, which is 25% of total) will be colour blind.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) 25% है। माँ वाहक (X^B X^b) है और पिता सामान्य (X^B Y) हैं। उनकी 25% संतान (वर्णांध पुत्र) वर्णांध होगी।

questions.text: डेंगू ज्वर का संवाहक है :
questions.text_english: The vector for dengue fever is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Female Aedes mosquito. Dengue fever is caused by the dengue virus and transmitted by the female Aedes aegypti mosquito. Female Anopheles mosquito is the vector for malaria; female Culex mosquito transmits filariasis. Male mosquitoes do not bite or transmit diseases as they feed on nectar.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) मादा एडीज़ मच्छर है। डेंगू ज्वर का वायरस मादा एडीज़ एजिप्टी मच्छर द्वारा फैलाया जाता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित जोड़ों में से कौन-सा सही सुमेलित नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). Monascus purpureus is a yeast used as a blood cholesterol-lowering agent (statins), not for citric acid production. Citric acid is produced by Aspergillus niger. The other pairs are correctly matched: Clostridium butylicum produces butyric acid; Trichoderma polysporum produces Cyclosporin A (an immunosuppressant); and Streptococcus produces Streptokinase (a clot-busting enzyme).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। Monascus purpureus साइट्रिक अम्ल नहीं बल्कि रक्त कोलेस्ट्रॉल कम करने वाले स्टेटिन का उत्पादन करता है। सिट्रिक अम्ल Aspergillus niger से प्राप्त होता है।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा प्लाज्मिडों का लक्षण नहीं है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following is not a feature of plasmids ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Single stranded. Plasmids are double-stranded circular DNA molecules. They are self-replicating (autonomous replication) and are extra-chromosomal (exist separately from the bacterial chromosome). They are NOT single-stranded; plasmids are always double-stranded DNA.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) एकल रज्जुक है। प्लाज्मिड द्विसूत्री वृत्ताकार DNA होते हैं, न कि एकसूत्री।

questions.text: समुद्र में जैवमात्रा का पिरामिड सामान्यत: उल्टा होता है क्योंकि समुद्र में :
questions.text_english: The pyramid of biomass in sea is generally inverted because in sea :

options.A: मछलियों की जैवमात्रा पादपप्लवकों की अपेक्षा अधिक होती है।
options.B: पादपप्लवकों की संख्या अपेक्षाकृत अधिक होती है।
options.C: पादपप्लवकों की संख्या अपेक्षाकृत कम होती है।
options.D: बड़ी मछलियाँ छोटी मछलियों को खाती हैं।

options_english.A: Biomass of fishes exceeds that of phytoplankton.
options_english.D: Large fishes feed on small fishes.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). In marine ecosystems, the pyramid of biomass is inverted because the total biomass of fishes (consumers) exceeds that of phytoplankton (producers) at any given time. Phytoplankton reproduce very rapidly and are consumed as quickly as they are produced, so their standing biomass is low at any instant even though their productivity is high. This means the producer level has less biomass than the consumer level, creating an inverted pyramid.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। समुद्र में फाइटोप्लैंक्टन की जैवमात्रा किसी भी समय बिंदु पर मछलियों की जैवमात्रा से कम होती है, इसलिए जैवमात्रा का पिरामिड उल्टा होता है।

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : आरएनए अस्थायी है तथा तीव्र गति से उत्परिवर्तित हो सकता है। कारण (R) : आरएनए के प्रत्येक न्यूक्लियोटाइड में 2'–OH समूह की उपस्थिति इसे अस्थायी तथा सरलता से विघटित होने वाला बनाती है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): RNA is unstable and can mutate at a faster rate. Reason (R): The presence of 2'-OH group in every nucleotide of RNA makes it labile and easily degradable.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) प्रश्न — नीचे दिए गए कोड में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Assertion-Reason question — select the correct answer from the codes given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. RNA is indeed unstable and mutates faster than DNA. The 2'-OH group present on every ribose sugar in RNA makes it chemically labile, prone to hydrolysis and degradation, which also contributes to its higher mutation rate. DNA lacks this 2'-OH group (it has 2'-H), making it more stable.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण, अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। RNA में 2'-OH समूह की उपस्थिति इसे अस्थायी और उत्परिवर्तनशील बनाती है।

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : विषाणु-संक्रमित कोशिकाएँ इन्टरफेरॉन उत्पन्न करती हैं। कारण (R) : इन्टरफेरॉन विषाणु-संक्रमित कोशिकाओं में शोथ (जलन) उत्पन्न कर सकते हैं।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): Virus-infected cells produce interferons. Reason (R): Interferons can cause inflammation of virus-infected cells.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) प्रश्न — नीचे दिए गए कोड में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The Assertion is true — virus-infected cells do produce interferons as part of the innate immune response. However, the Reason is false — interferons do not cause inflammation of virus-infected cells. Instead, interferons protect non-infected neighbouring cells by signalling them to activate antiviral defenses, inhibiting viral replication. The Reason incorrectly describes the action of interferons.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। अभिकथन सत्य है (विषाणु-संक्रमित कोशिकाएँ इन्टरफेरॉन बनाती हैं), लेकिन कारण असत्य है (इन्टरफेरॉन शोथ नहीं, बल्कि पड़ोसी कोशिकाओं को विषाणु से सुरक्षित करते हैं)।

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : जीवों की कोशिकाओं से डीएनए पृथक् करने के लिए कोशिका भित्ति को विघटित करने हेतु विशिष्ट एंज़ाइमों का उपयोग किया जाता है। कारण (R) : एंज़ाइम सेलूलेज़ द्वारा कवक कोशिका भित्ति का विघटन किया जाता है।

questions.text_english:
(a) Name any two copper releasing intra-uterine devices. State two reasons that make them effective contraceptives.

OR

(b) Name any two outbreeding devices that flowering plants have developed and explain how they help in encouraging cross-pollination.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

key_points: (a) CuT and Cu7 are two copper-releasing IUDs. They work by making the uterine environment hostile to sperm motility and by inhibiting fertilization.
(b) Self-incompatibility and unisexuality (dioecy) are two outbreeding devices that prevent self-pollination and promote cross-pollination.

questions.solution:
Answer (a): Two copper-releasing intra-uterine devices are CuT and Cu7. They are effective contraceptives because copper ions released suppress sperm motility and their fertilising capacity, and they also make the uterine endometrium unfavourable for implantation. These dual actions make copper IUDs highly effective.

Answer (b): Two outbreeding devices are (i) Self-incompatibility — the pollen of a flower is unable to germinate on the stigma of the same flower or same plant due to biochemical recognition mechanisms, thus forcing the plant to rely on pollen from another individual. (ii) Unisexuality (Dioecy) — plants may bear either only male flowers or only female flowers, making self-pollination impossible and ensuring that pollination must occur between two separate individuals, thereby promoting cross-pollination.
questions.solution_hindi:
उत्तर (क): दो कॉपर-मोचित अंत:गर्भाशयी युक्तियाँ — CuT और Cu7 हैं। ये शुक्राणु की गतिशीलता को रोककर और गर्भाशय के अंत:स्तर को प्रतिकूल बनाकर गर्भनिरोध करती हैं।

questions.text_english: Although Haemophilia and sickle cell anemia are two blood related Mendelian disorders, yet, they differ in their pattern of inheritance. State any two differences.

key_points: Haemophilia is X-linked recessive; Sickle cell anemia is autosomal recessive.
Haemophilia predominantly affects males; Sickle cell anemia affects both sexes equally.

questions.solution: Haemophilia and sickle cell anemia differ in their inheritance pattern in two important ways. First, haemophilia is an X-linked recessive disorder, meaning the defective gene is located on the X chromosome and therefore the disease predominantly affects males, while females act as carriers. Sickle cell anemia, on the other hand, is an autosomal recessive disorder — the defective gene is located on an autosome, so it affects both males and females equally. Second, in haemophilia, a carrier female (heterozygous) is phenotypically normal, whereas in sickle cell anemia, a heterozygous individual shows sickle cell trait (partial expression), not the full disease.
questions.solution_hindi: हीमोफीलिया लिंग-सहलग्न (X-लिंक्ड) अप्रभावी विकार है जो मुख्यतः पुरुषों को प्रभावित करता है। सिकल सेल एनिमिया कायिक गुणसूत्र (ऑटोसोमल) अप्रभावी विकार है जो स्त्री और पुरुष दोनों को समान रूप से प्रभावित करता है।

questions.text_english: Write the role of 'ori' and restriction site in the cloning vector pBR322.

key_points: ori (Origin of Replication): allows autonomous replication of the vector and inserted foreign DNA within the host cell.
Restriction site: provides a specific location where restriction enzymes can cut the vector to insert foreign DNA.

questions.solution: In the cloning vector pBR322, the 'ori' (origin of replication) is the specific DNA sequence from which replication of the vector begins. It controls the copy number of the vector in the host cell and ensures that the recombinant DNA (vector + foreign insert) is replicated and maintained in the host cell. The restriction site is a specific nucleotide sequence where restriction endonucleases cut the vector DNA. This allows foreign DNA to be inserted at that precise location to create recombinant DNA. pBR322 has multiple restriction sites located within its antibiotic resistance genes (ampR and tetR), which also enable insertional inactivation for identification of recombinants.
questions.solution_hindi: pBR322 में 'ori' प्रतिकृति का उद्गम स्थल है जो परपोषी कोशिका में संवाहक एवं उसमें जुड़े विजातीय DNA की प्रतिकृति सुनिश्चित करता है। प्रतिबंधन स्थल वह विशेष अनुक्रम है जहाँ प्रतिबंधन एंडोन्यूक्लिएज़ DNA को काटता है और विजातीय DNA को जोड़ने की अनुमति देता है।

questions.text: अपरद की प्रकृति तथा ताप, अपघटन की दर को किस प्रकार प्रभावित करते हैं ?
questions.text_english: How is the rate of decomposition affected by the nature of detritus and temperature ?

key_points: Nature of detritus: detritus rich in lignin and chitin decomposes slowly; detritus rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances decomposes faster.
Temperature: higher temperatures (within optimal range) increase decomposition rate; low temperatures slow it down due to reduced microbial activity.

questions.solution: The rate of decomposition is influenced by both the nature of detritus and temperature. Regarding nature of detritus: detritus with a high content of lignin and chitin decomposes slowly because these compounds are chemically resistant to microbial degradation. In contrast, detritus that is rich in nitrogen and contains easily soluble substances decomposes rapidly. Warm, moist detritus also decompose faster. Regarding temperature: decomposition is faster at higher temperatures (within an optimal range) because the enzymatic activity of decomposers increases with temperature. At very low temperatures, microbial activity is greatly reduced, slowing decomposition significantly, as seen in tundra regions.
questions.solution_hindi: अपरद की प्रकृति: लिग्निन और काइटिन युक्त अपरद धीरे अपघटित होता है; नाइट्रोजन-समृद्ध अपरद शीघ्र अपघटित होता है। ताप: उच्च ताप पर अपघटकों की एंज़ाइमी क्रियाशीलता बढ़ती है, अत: अपघटन तेज होता है; निम्न ताप पर अपघटन धीमा पड़ जाता है।

(क) 'पात्रे निषेचन (आईवीएफ)' को यह नाम क्यों दिया गया है ? इसका महत्त्व लिखिए।

questions.text_english:
(a) Why is 'in vitro fertilization (IVF)' so named? State its importance.

(b) Distinguish between GIFT and ZIFT.

key_points: IVF is named so because fertilization occurs outside the body (in glass/lab).
IVF is important for couples who cannot conceive naturally due to infertility.
GIFT transfers gametes (ova and sperm) into the fallopian tube; ZIFT transfers a zygote or early embryo into the fallopian tube.

questions.solution:
Answer (a): IVF stands for 'in vitro fertilization'. It is so named because 'in vitro' is a Latin term meaning 'in glass', and in this technique, fertilization of the egg by the sperm takes place outside the body of the woman — in a laboratory dish or test tube. The fertilized egg (embryo) is then transferred into the uterus. Its importance lies in helping infertile couples who cannot conceive naturally due to blocked fallopian tubes, low sperm count, or other reproductive issues, to have children.

Answer (b): GIFT (Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer) involves the transfer of an unfertilized egg along with sperm directly into the fallopian tube of the woman, where fertilization is expected to occur naturally inside the body. ZIFT (Zygote Intra Fallopian Transfer) involves the fertilization of the egg outside the body (in vitro), and the resulting zygote or early embryo (up to 8 cells) is then transferred into the fallopian tube. So the key difference is that in GIFT, fertilization occurs inside the body, while in ZIFT, fertilization is done outside the body.
questions.solution_hindi: IVF में 'in vitro' का अर्थ 'काँच में' है अर्थात निषेचन शरीर के बाहर प्रयोगशाला में होता है। यह निसंतान दम्पतियों के लिए महत्त्वपूर्ण है। GIFT में असंसेचित अंडाणु व शुक्राणु फैलोपियन नलिका में स्थानांतरित किए जाते हैं; ZIFT में पात्रे बने युग्मज को फैलोपियन नलिका में स्थानांतरित किया जाता है।

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Write the karyotype and the genetic disorder of an individual who has developed from a zygote formed from an 'XX' egg fertilised by a 'Y' sperm.
(ii) Mention any two symptoms of this genetic disorder.
(iii) Write the possible reason that leads to the formation of this 'XX' egg.

OR

(b) In case of any dispute, a very small sample of tissue or even a drop of blood can help us to determine the paternity of a child. Provide a scientific explanation to substantiate the statement.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

key_points: (a)(i) Karyotype: 47, XXY; Disorder: Klinefelter's Syndrome.
(a)(ii) Symptoms: Gynaecomastia (development of breasts in males), sterility/infertility.
(a)(iii) Non-disjunction of sex chromosomes during oogenesis produces XX egg.
(b) DNA fingerprinting from tissue/blood can uniquely identify individuals and match parental DNA.

questions.solution:
Answer (a): (i) When an XX egg is fertilised by a Y sperm, the resulting individual has the karyotype 47, XXY and suffers from Klinefelter's Syndrome. (ii) Two symptoms of Klinefelter's Syndrome are: gynaecomastia (abnormal development of breast tissue in males) and sterility (the individual is infertile due to very small, poorly developed testes). (iii) The XX egg is formed due to non-disjunction of sex chromosomes during meiosis I or meiosis II in oogenesis. When the two X chromosomes fail to separate properly during meiosis, both X chromosomes pass into the same egg cell, resulting in an XX egg.

Answer (b): DNA fingerprinting (DNA profiling) is the scientific technique that can determine paternity from a tiny tissue sample or a drop of blood. Every individual's DNA has unique repetitive sequences called Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTRs). Since a child inherits half of its DNA from each parent, the child's DNA fingerprint will show bands that match partly with the mother's and partly with the father's profile. By comparing the DNA fingerprint of the child with the alleged father, paternity can be conclusively established or ruled out.

questions.text:
(क) स्थानांतरण (रूपांतरण) प्रक्रम के दौरान उस प्रक्रम की व्याख्या कीजिए जिसमें ऐमीनो अम्ल अंतरण आरएनए (tRNA) अणु से जुड़ता है।
(ख) स्थानांतरण के इस प्रक्रम का समापन कैसे होता है ?
(ग) 'यूटीआर (UTR)' का विस्तृत रूप लिखिए। वे कहाँ अवस्थित होते हैं ?
questions.text_english:
(a) Explain the process by which amino acid gets attached to the tRNA molecule during translation process.
(b) How does the translation process get terminated?
(c) Expand 'UTR'. Where are they located ?

key_points: (a) Aminoacylation of tRNA: amino acid is activated and attached to its specific tRNA by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase using ATP energy.
(b) Termination: when a stop codon (UAA, UAG, UGA) enters the A-site, release factors cause the polypeptide to be released.
(c) UTR = Untranslated Region; located at both the 5' end and 3' end of mRNA.

questions.solution:
Answer (a): During translation, amino acids are activated and attached to their specific tRNA molecules in a process called aminoacylation (or charging of tRNA). This is carried out by a specific enzyme called aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase. Using energy from ATP (two high-energy phosphate bonds are used), the enzyme catalyses the attachment of the specific amino acid to the 3' end of its corresponding tRNA, forming aminoacyl-tRNA. There are at least 20 different aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, one for each amino acid.

Answer (b): The translation process terminates when one of the three stop codons (UAA, UAG, or UGA) appears at the A-site of the ribosome. These codons are not recognized by any tRNA but are instead recognized by proteins called release factors. The release factors stimulate hydrolysis of the bond between the polypeptide chain and the tRNA at the P-site, causing the polypeptide to be released. The ribosome then dissociates into its subunits.

Answer (c): UTR stands for Untranslated Region. UTRs are sequences present in the mRNA that are transcribed but not translated into protein. They are located at both ends of the mRNA: the 5' UTR is found before the start codon (AUG) and the 3' UTR is found after the stop codon. They play important roles in regulation of translation and mRNA stability.
questions.solution_hindi: (क) ऐमीनोऐसिल-tRNA सिंथेटेज़ एंज़ाइम ATP की ऊर्जा से ऐमीनो अम्ल को उसके विशिष्ट tRNA से जोड़ता है — इसे tRNA का ऐमीनोएसिलेशन कहते हैं। (ख) जब A-स्थल पर स्टॉप कोडन (UAA, UAG, UGA) आता है, तो मुक्ति कारक पॉलीपेप्टाइड को tRNA से अलग कर देते हैं। (ग) UTR = अनुवाद-रहित क्षेत्र (Untranslated Region); ये mRNA के 5' और 3' दोनों सिरों पर होते हैं।

questions.text_english:
(a) Differentiate between humoral immune response and cell-mediated immune response.
(b) Draw a schematic diagram of an antibody molecule and label any four parts.

key_points: Humoral: mediated by B-lymphocytes; produces antibodies; effective against extracellular pathogens.
Cell-mediated: mediated by T-lymphocytes; no antibody production; effective against intracellular pathogens and transplant rejection.
Antibody diagram parts: heavy chain, light chain, antigen-binding site, variable region, constant region, hinge region.

questions.solution:
Answer (a): Humoral immune response is mediated by B-lymphocytes (B-cells). When activated, B-cells differentiate into plasma cells which produce specific antibodies (immunoglobulins) that circulate in the blood and lymph, binding to and neutralising pathogens such as bacteria and viruses present outside the cells. Cell-mediated immune response is mediated by T-lymphocytes (T-cells), particularly cytotoxic T-cells. It does not involve antibody production. Instead, T-cells directly attack and destroy infected cells, cancer cells, and transplanted organs. It is especially effective against intracellular pathogens like viruses and is responsible for graft rejection.

Answer (b): An antibody (immunoglobulin) molecule has a Y-shaped structure. It consists of four polypeptide chains — two identical heavy (H) chains and two identical light (L) chains — held together by disulfide bonds. The four parts that should be labelled are: (1) Heavy chain, (2) Light chain, (3) Antigen-binding site (variable region at the tips of the Y), (4) Constant region (the stem of the Y) / alternatively, the hinge region.

questions.text_english:
The picture given below shows:
(a) Roots of a typical control tobacco crop plant (infected).
(b) Transgenic tobacco plant showing healthy roots even after deliberate infection by nematode.
Explain how this transformation was achieved in the tobacco plant.

key_points: RNA interference (RNAi) technology was used.
Nematode-specific genes were introduced that produce dsRNA to silence parasite genes.
The nematode cannot survive in the transgenic plant.

questions.solution: The transformation in the transgenic tobacco plant was achieved using the technique of RNA Interference (RNAi). Scientists used Agrobacterium tumefaciens as a vector to introduce a specific nematode gene into the tobacco plant in such a way that it produced double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) complementary to a vital gene of the nematode Meloidogyne incognita. When the nematode feeds on the roots of this transgenic tobacco plant, the dsRNA enters the nematode's cells. This dsRNA then triggers RNAi — it binds to the complementary mRNA of the nematode's essential gene and causes its silencing (degradation), preventing its translation. As a result, the nematode cannot produce the essential protein it needs for survival, so it dies, and the plant's roots remain healthy and undamaged even after deliberate nematode infection.
questions.solution_hindi: यह रूपांतरण RNA इन्टरफेरेंस (RNAi) तकनीक द्वारा प्राप्त किया गया। सूत्रकृमि-विशिष्ट जीन को Agrobacterium की सहायता से तंबाकू में डाला गया जिससे dsRNA बनता है। जब सूत्रकृमि पादप की मूलें खाता है तो यह dsRNA उसके जीन को साइलेंस कर देता है और सूत्रकृमि मर जाता है।

questions.text_english: Predation is referred to as a detrimental interaction. Explain any three positive roles, supported by an example each, that a predator plays in an ecosystem.

key_points: Predators control prey population, preventing overgrazing (e.g., wolves controlling deer populations).
Predators maintain species diversity by preventing competitive exclusion (e.g., sea otters keeping sea urchin populations in check).
Predators aid energy transfer through food chains and maintain ecosystem balance.

questions.solution: Although predation appears harmful to prey species, predators play several important positive roles in an ecosystem. First, predators control the population of their prey and prevent overpopulation. For example, wolves in Yellowstone National Park keep the deer population in check, preventing overgrazing of vegetation. Second, predators help maintain species diversity in an ecosystem. Without predators, competitively dominant prey species would multiply unchecked and drive other species to extinction. For example, sea otters prey on sea urchins; without sea otters, sea urchins would overpopulate and destroy kelp forests, eliminating the habitat of many other species. Third, predators remove weak, sick, or aged individuals from prey populations (acting as a natural selector), which keeps prey populations healthy and genetically fit. For example, lions preferentially hunt weak or old wildebeest, maintaining the overall health of the prey population.

sub_questions.text_english:
State the site of action of FSH in the testes and describe its action thereafter.

OR

Describe the role of LH in the process of spermatogenesis.

key_points: FSH acts on Sertoli cells, stimulating them to secrete factors that aid spermatogenesis.
LH acts on Leydig cells (interstitial cells), stimulating them to produce testosterone, which promotes spermatogenesis.

sub_questions.solution:
Answer (FSH): FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone) acts on the Sertoli cells present in the seminiferous tubules of the testes. After binding to Sertoli cells, FSH stimulates them to secrete various paracrine factors and androgen-binding protein (ABP), which help maintain the local concentration of testosterone at levels necessary to support and promote spermatogenesis.

Answer (LH): LH (Luteinising Hormone) acts on the Leydig cells (interstitial cells of Leydig) located in the connective tissue between the seminiferous tubules. LH stimulates the Leydig cells to synthesize and secrete testosterone (male sex hormone/androgen). Testosterone then acts on the Sertoli cells and spermatogenic cells to promote and maintain spermatogenesis.

key_points: (i) Spermatogonia undergo mitosis and differentiation to produce primary spermatocytes.
(ii) Primary spermatocytes undergo Meiosis I to produce secondary spermatocytes; secondary spermatocytes undergo Meiosis II to produce spermatids.

sub_questions.solution: (i) Spermatogonia undergo mitosis to increase in number and then differentiate into primary spermatocytes. (ii) Primary spermatocytes undergo Meiosis I (reductional division) to produce two secondary spermatocytes. Secondary spermatocytes then undergo Meiosis II (equational division) to produce four spermatids, which subsequently mature into spermatozoa (sperms).

In 1981, the health workers of United States of America had become aware of the increased frequency of Kaposi's sarcoma, cancer of the skin and blood vessels and another disease pneumocystis pneumonia, a respiratory infection caused by a protozoan. Both these diseases were very rare in the general population, but occurred frequently in more severely immunosuppressed individuals. This led to the recognition of the immune system disorder that was named Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS).

In 1983, virologists working in the USA and France had identified a causative agent for 'AIDS', now known as Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV). 'HIV' follows a set path to attack the human body to cause the disease.
questions.solution: Passage-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text: मानव शरीर में प्रवेश करने के पश्चात् एचआईवी जिस कोशिका समूह पर आक्रमण करता है, उसका नाम लिखिए। इस कोशिका में होने वाली विभिन्न परिघटनाओं को लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Name the group of cells the HIV attacks after gaining entry into the human body and write the various events that occur within this cell.

key_points: HIV attacks T-helper lymphocytes (CD4+ T-cells / macrophages).

Events: HIV uses reverse transcriptase to make DNA from its RNA; viral DNA integrates into host cell genome; produces new viral RNA and proteins; new virions bud off and infect more cells; T-cell count decreases leading to immunodeficiency.

sub_questions.solution: HIV attacks the T-helper lymphocytes (CD4+ T-cells) and also macrophages after entering the human body. Within the T-helper cells, the following events occur: HIV uses its enzyme reverse transcriptase to synthesize double-stranded viral DNA from its RNA genome. This viral DNA then integrates into the host cell's chromosome with the help of integrase enzyme, becoming a provirus. The provirus uses the host cell machinery to produce new viral RNA and viral proteins. These assemble into new HIV particles (virions) that bud off from the host cell, ultimately destroying it. As more T-helper cells are destroyed and their number progressively declines, the person's immune system weakens and they become susceptible to opportunistic infections.

key_points: ELISA: Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay.
Treatment: Anti-retroviral therapy (ART) using drugs like AZT (Zidovudine); no complete cure exists.

sub_questions.solution: The diagnostic test used for detecting AIDS is ELISA, which stands for Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay. This test detects the presence of HIV antibodies in the blood of the patient. As of now, there is no complete cure for AIDS. The possible treatment available is Anti-Retroviral Therapy (ART), which involves a combination of antiretroviral drugs such as Zidovudine (AZT), which inhibit the reverse transcriptase enzyme of HIV, thereby slowing down viral replication and the progression of the disease. However, ART only manages the disease; it does not eliminate HIV from the body.

sub_questions.text_english:
Mention any two steps suggested by WHO for preventing the spread of this disease.

OR

'A patient suffering from AIDS does not die of this disease but from some other infection.' Justify the statement.

key_points: WHO steps: (1) Use of safe blood and blood products; (2) Promotion of safe sex / use of condoms; education and awareness campaigns.

Justification: HIV destroys T-helper cells, causing severe immunodeficiency. The patient then succumbs to opportunistic infections (like tuberculosis, pneumonia) that a healthy immune system would normally control.

sub_questions.solution:
Answer (WHO steps): Two steps suggested by WHO to prevent the spread of AIDS are: (1) Ensuring safe blood transfusion by screening all donated blood for HIV before use. (2) Promoting safe sexual practices including use of condoms and advocating for faithful monogamous relationships; also creating awareness about the dangers of sharing needles and syringes among intravenous drug users.

Answer (Justification): The statement is justified because HIV does not directly kill the patient — rather, HIV gradually destroys the T-helper lymphocytes (CD4+ T-cells), which are central to the immune response. As the count of T-helper cells drops to critically low levels, the patient's immune system becomes severely compromised and unable to fight even minor infections. The patient then dies from opportunistic infections such as tuberculosis, Pneumocystis pneumonia, or other infections caused by organisms that would normally be controlled by a healthy immune system — hence death is caused by these secondary infections, not HIV itself.

questions.text_english:
(a)
(i) Explain the process of double fertilization in an angiosperm starting from the germination of pollen grains on the stigma, mentioning the ploidy of the end products formed at the end. State the role of synergids during the course of the process.
(ii) Why does the development of endosperm precede that of the embryo?

OR

(b)
(i) Mention the site where fertilisation of the ovum occurs in a human female. Explain the process of fertilization and mention how polyspermy is prevented.
(ii) Name the embryonic stage that gets implanted in the uterus. Explain the process of implantation in a human female.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

key_points: (a)(i) Pollen germinates on stigma; pollen tube grows through style guided by synergids; two male gametes released; one fuses with egg (syngamy, diploid zygote 2n); one fuses with polar nuclei (triple fusion, triploid PEN 3n) — double fertilization.
(a)(ii) Endosperm provides nutrition to the developing embryo.
(b)(i) Fertilization occurs in the ampullary region of the fallopian tube. Acrosome reaction; zona pellucida depolarization prevents polyspermy.
(b)(ii) Blastocyst implants in uterus; trophoblast cells proliferate and embed in endometrium.

questions.solution:
Answer (a)(i): When pollen grains land on the stigma of a compatible flower, they germinate. The pollen tube grows through the style towards the ovule, directed by chemical signals from the synergid cells of the embryo sac. The tube enters the embryo sac through the micropyle and releases two male gametes. One male gamete (n) fuses with the egg cell (n), a process called syngamy, producing the diploid zygote (2n). The other male gamete (n) fuses with the two polar nuclei (n+n) of the central cell, a process called triple fusion, forming the triploid (3n) primary endosperm nucleus. Since two fusions occur, this is called double fertilization — a unique feature of angiosperms. The role of synergids: synergids secrete chemotropic substances that guide the pollen tube toward the embryo sac; they also help in pollen tube entry and release of male gametes into the embryo sac.

Answer (a)(ii): Endosperm development precedes that of the embryo because the developing embryo is a heterotroph that requires nutrients for its growth and differentiation. The endosperm acts as the primary nutritive tissue for the embryo; it must be ready before the embryo begins active cell division and differentiation, ensuring a continuous supply of nutrients to the embryo.

Answer (b)(i): Fertilization of the ovum in a human female occurs in the ampullary region of the fallopian tube (ampulla). After ovulation, the secondary oocyte is released from the Graafian follicle and enters the fallopian tube. A sperm cell that reaches the egg undergoes the acrosome reaction, releasing enzymes that digest the zona pellucida (acrosomal enzymes). The sperm fuses with the egg membrane, stimulating the completion of meiosis II in the secondary oocyte, producing the mature ovum and a second polar body. The fusion of the sperm nucleus and egg nucleus forms the diploid zygote. Polyspermy is prevented by cortical granule reaction: upon entry of the first sperm, calcium ions are released from the ER of the egg, triggering cortical granules to fuse with the plasma membrane and release enzymes that harden the zona pellucida (zona reaction), preventing further sperm from penetrating.

Answer (b)(ii): The embryonic stage that implants in the uterus is the blastocyst. After fertilization, the zygote undergoes cleavage as it moves through the fallopian tube. By the time it reaches the uterus (around 5-6 days after fertilization), it has become a blastocyst — a hollow ball of cells with an outer trophoblast layer and an inner cell mass (embryoblast). During implantation, the trophoblast cells proliferate rapidly and secrete enzymes that digest the uterine endometrium. The blastocyst embeds into the endometrium, and the trophoblast cells differentiate into syncytiotrophoblast (which invades deeper into the endometrium) and cytotrophoblast, establishing the early placenta. The inner cell mass (embryoblast) will subsequently develop into the embryo.

(a)
(i) Compare the pattern of inheritance of flower colour in garden pea plant (violet/white) with snapdragon plant (red/white) on the basis of the following:
(1) F1 phenotypic expression;
(2) expected phenotypic and genotypic expression of F2 generation;
(3) the conclusion you reached at the end of the comparison made.
(ii) List any two characteristics of pattern of inheritance of human blood group ABO.

OR

(b)
(i) Draw a schematic, self-explanatory labelled diagram of lac operon in 'switched on condition'.
(ii) Why is regulation of lac operon referred to as negative regulation?
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

key_points: (a)(i)(1) Garden pea F1: all violet (complete dominance); Snapdragon F1: all pink (incomplete dominance).
(a)(i)(2) Garden pea F2: 3 violet : 1 white (3:1 phenotypic; 1:2:1 genotypic); Snapdragon F2: 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white (1:2:1 phenotypic and genotypic).
(a)(i)(3) Conclusion: Garden pea shows complete dominance; snapdragon shows incomplete dominance.
(a)(ii) ABO shows co-dominance and multiple allelism.
(b)(i) Lac operon switched on diagram: when lactose is present, it binds to repressor, inactivating it, allowing RNA polymerase to transcribe structural genes.
(b)(ii) Negative regulation: in the absence of inducer, an active repressor blocks gene expression.

questions.solution:
Answer (a)(i): In garden pea, when violet-flowered (VV) plants are crossed with white-flowered (vv) plants: F1 generation — all plants show violet colour because violet (V) is completely dominant over white (v). F2 generation — phenotypic ratio is 3 violet : 1 white; genotypic ratio is 1 VV : 2 Vv : 1 vv.

In snapdragon, when red-flowered (RR) plants are crossed with white-flowered (rr) plants: F1 generation — all plants show pink colour because neither allele is completely dominant; the heterozygote (Rr) shows an intermediate phenotype (incomplete dominance). F2 generation — phenotypic ratio is 1 red (RR) : 2 pink (Rr) : 1 white (rr); genotypic ratio is the same 1:2:1.

Conclusion: Garden pea shows complete dominance where one allele completely masks the expression of the other, giving 3:1 phenotypic ratio in F2. Snapdragon shows incomplete dominance where neither allele is completely dominant, and the heterozygote shows an intermediate phenotype, giving a 1:2:1 phenotypic ratio identical to the genotypic ratio in F2. This challenged the classical Mendelian concept of dominance.

Answer (a)(ii): Two characteristics of the pattern of inheritance of human ABO blood groups are: (i) It exhibits multiple allelism — the trait is controlled by three alleles (IA, IB, and i) for a single gene locus, though an individual carries only two alleles. (ii) It shows co-dominance — when both IA and IB alleles are present together in a person (genotype IAIB), both are equally expressed, producing blood group AB, without any masking of either allele.

Answer (b)(i): In the lac operon switched-on condition (when lactose is present): Lactose (the inducer) binds to the repressor protein, causing a conformational change that prevents the repressor from binding to the operator. With the operator free, RNA polymerase can bind to the promoter and transcribe the structural genes (lacZ coding for beta-galactosidase, lacY coding for permease, and lacA coding for transacetylase). [A labelled diagram should show: promoter, operator, structural genes lacZ, lacY, lacA, RNA polymerase on DNA, inactive repressor with lactose bound, and mRNA being transcribed.]

Answer (b)(ii): The regulation of lac operon is called negative regulation because, in the absence of the inducer (lactose), the repressor protein is active and binds to the operator region, thereby switching off (negatively regulating) the transcription of the structural genes. The default state of the operon is 'off' — the repressor actively prevents gene expression. Only when the inducer (lactose) is present does it inactivate the repressor, relieving this negative regulation and allowing transcription.

questions.text_english:
(a)
(i) Why should a cell be made competent to take up an alien DNA? How can a bacterial cell be made competent using calcium ions? Explain.
(ii)
(1) State the importance of gel electrophoresis in biotechnology.
(2) Explain the principle on which this technique works.
(3) Mention why ethidium bromide is used in this technique.

OR

(b) 'Bt cotton', the genetically modified crop, has greatly helped the cotton farmers to increase their crop yield.
(i) How was Bt cotton plant made resistant to bollworm? Explain.
(ii) Describe the mechanism that leads to the death of bollworms feeding on Bt cotton plants.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any one of the following.

key_points: (a)(i) Cells are naturally impermeable to foreign DNA; Ca2+ ions increase cell wall permeability allowing DNA uptake.
(a)(ii)(1) Gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments by size for analysis.
(a)(ii)(2) Principle: DNA is negatively charged; moves toward anode through gel; smaller fragments move faster.
(a)(ii)(3) Ethidium bromide intercalates into DNA and fluoresces under UV light to visualize bands.
(b)(i) Bt toxin gene (cry genes) from Bacillus thuringiensis was inserted into cotton.
(b)(ii) Bt toxin is in inactive protoxin form; in bollworm gut (alkaline pH), it becomes active, binds to midgut epithelium, creates pores, causing cell lysis and death.

questions.solution:
Answer (a)(i): A cell must be made competent to take up foreign (alien) DNA because the cell wall and plasma membrane act as physical and chemical barriers that prevent the entry of large foreign DNA molecules into the cell. To introduce recombinant DNA into bacteria, the cell must be rendered permeable. Using calcium ions (Ca2+), bacterial cells can be made competent as follows: bacterial cells are incubated in an ice-cold solution of calcium chloride (CaCl2). The Ca2+ ions weaken the cell wall and alter the membrane properties, making the cell transiently permeable to DNA. The cells are then given a brief heat shock (at 42°C for 90 seconds) which drives the DNA through the membrane pores into the cell. This whole process is called chemical transformation or heat shock method.

Answer (a)(ii)(1): Gel electrophoresis is essential in biotechnology for separating and analyzing DNA fragments of different sizes after restriction enzyme digestion. It is used to confirm the presence and size of the inserted gene in recombinant DNA, in DNA fingerprinting, and in molecular diagnostics.

(2) Principle: DNA is a negatively charged molecule. When an electric current is applied across a gel (usually agarose), DNA fragments migrate from the negative pole (cathode) toward the positive pole (anode). Smaller DNA fragments move faster and travel farther through the gel matrix, while larger fragments move more slowly. This separates fragments by size, creating a pattern of bands at different positions in the gel.

(3) Ethidium bromide (EtBr) is a fluorescent dye used to visualize DNA bands. EtBr intercalates between the base pairs of the DNA double helix. When the gel is exposed to UV (ultraviolet) light, the ethidium bromide-stained DNA bands fluoresce bright orange, making the position and amount of DNA fragments visible.

Answer (b)(i): Bt cotton was made resistant to bollworm (Helicoverpa armigera / boll weevil) using genetic engineering. Specific genes called cry genes (e.g., cry1Ac and cry2Ab) were isolated from the soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt). These cry genes encode insecticidal crystal proteins (Bt toxins / delta endotoxins). Using Agrobacterium-mediated gene transfer, these cry genes were introduced and integrated into the cotton plant's genome. The transgenic cotton plants now produce the Bt toxin protein in their tissues, making them resistant to bollworm attack.

Answer (b)(ii): In Bacillus thuringiensis and in the transgenic Bt cotton plant, the Bt toxin exists as an inactive protoxin (pro-Bt toxin). When a bollworm (caterpillar) feeds on Bt cotton, it ingests the inactive protoxin along with the plant tissue. In the alkaline environment of the insect's midgut, the protoxin is solubilized and converted into its active toxic form by gut proteases. The activated Bt toxin then binds to specific receptor proteins on the epithelial cells lining the midgut of the insect. This binding creates pores in the cell membrane, disrupting the osmotic balance and causing cell swelling and lysis (cell death). The destruction of midgut epithelial cells leads to paralysis of the insect's digestive system; the bollworm stops feeding and eventually dies.
